lawRefs: Rev. Proc. 2025-25 (applicable percentage table and 9.96% required contribution percentage for 2026)
26 U.S.C. 36B(b)(3)(A) (original, indexed table; the ARPA sec. 9661 / IRA sec. 12001 enhanced table applied only to tax years 2021-2025)
26 U.S.C. 36B(c)(1)(A) (household income 100%-400% of the poverty line; the 2021-2025 suspension of the 400% limit has expired)
Pub. L. 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) sec. 71305: 26 U.S.C. 36B(f)(2)(B) repayment limitation repealed for tax years beginning after 2025
header.notes: Law in force for coverage year 2026: the enhanced ARPA/IRA credits expired on 2025-12-31 and were not extended (a House-passed three-year extension was never enacted), so the original indexed table applies and there is no credit above 400% FPL. Within each band the percentage rises linearly from `initial` to `final`. The first band ("less than 133%") starts at 0 for contiguity; eligibility starts at `minFpl`. Contract caveat: by statute a household at EXACTLY 400% FPL is still eligible ("not more than 400%"); the cliff is strictly above `cliffFpl`. Excess advance credit is repaid in full (no caps) from tax year 2026, per the IRS premium tax credit Q&A. Not modelled: OBBBA changes to eligibility of certain lawfully present immigrants. sha256 is of the raw source document as downloaded.
